author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Fire departments and residents across southern New Hampshire gathered to honor Raymond firefighter Eric Phillips during a dignified transfer from Concord on Sunday.

Phillips, 44, died Friday night after suffering a medical emergency while responding to a call for service, according to reporting compiled by the Daily Dispatch from WMUR. The transfer began shortly after 4:30 p.m. in Concord, and more than a dozen departments took part in the procession.

Firefighters positioned apparatus on Route 101 overpasses as the procession traveled toward Raymond. Community members also stood along the route. The coordinated display followed a long emergency-services tradition of accompanying a fallen responder and visibly supporting the person’s family and department.

Phillips had served with the Raymond Fire Department for five years. The public observance brought together departments that routinely assist one another across town lines, especially during large fires and other emergencies. Officials had not announced additional public memorial arrangements in the source report. Residents should rely on the Raymond Fire Department or town notices for any later service information.
dek: More than a dozen departments joined a dignified transfer for Eric Phillips, who died after a medical emergency while responding to a call.
headline: New Hampshire fire departments honor fallen Raymond firefighter
